_readme: DATED provider catalog for `orc extra`. Providers, NEVER models.
Between this package's cutoff and any given release the model lineup moves:
DeepSeek V3.2 -> V4, Kimi K2 -> K2.7, GLM 4.6 -> 5.2, MiniMax M2 -> M2.7,
Qwen 3 -> 3.6, MiMo v2 -> v2.5. A SHIPPED MODEL LIST IS WRONG WITHIN A
QUARTER, and wrong SILENTLY: a user picks from a stale dropdown and gets a
404 in the middle of a wave. So model ids come from the provider's own
/v1/models at ping time and are cached in the profile (`models_seen`).
`as_of` is load-bearing, exactly like bin/pricing.json: a catalog older than
90 days prints a staleness warning beside every provider listing. Bump the
date only when you have re-checked the base URLs against each provider's
own docs.
`auth_env` names the ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE, not a header. Claude Code picks
the header FROM the variable you set: ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN -> `Authorization:
Bearer`, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -> `x-api-key`. Ollama's Anthropic endpoint
REJECTS x-api-key, so a row that said `bearer` plus a resolver that set
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY would fail at 401 with nothing on screen explaining why.
`api_base` (OpenAI-compatible, engine `api`) and `anthropic_base` (the
/anthropic shim, engine `claude-shim`) are INDEPENDENTLY probeable: they are
different URLs with different capabilities, and `/v1/models` does not
necessarily live under the shim one.
`custom` is a real row and is the escape hatch that keeps this catalog from
being a gate: anything OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible works by typing a
base URL, with no entry here.

`provider_routing` marks a provider that accepts an OpenRouter-style `provider` block in the request body (zdr, data_collection, require_parameters, only, allow_fallbacks). Only engine `api` composes a body, so this is the ONE enforceable privacy control in the whole subsystem — and it exists on the aggregator, plus `custom` because a custom base URL is routinely an aggregator-compatible gateway. Everything else gets `orc extra privacy` REFUSED BY NAME rather than an unknown body field that 400s mid-wave.
`cli_bin` names the LOCAL BINARY a provider's only surface is. A row that
carries it is a tool that may simply not be installed, which is a state
before it is a failure: `orc extra tools` computes it fresh on every read
(never stored — a stored `installing` flag is a lie the moment the user hits
Ctrl-C), and `orc extra add --provider <that row>` REFUSES while it is
absent, naming the install command instead of creating a profile that cannot
work.
`install` is per platform and per package manager and it AGES WITH THIS FILE.
The common failure is `npm i -g codex`, which installs an unrelated 2012
package — so the exact string has to come from here rather than from memory,
and it is dated for the same reason a base URL is.
`no_install_alternative` is an asymmetry made data: a provider whose tool is
absent may have an install-free route (an ordinary `api` row serving the same
models), or it may not. `null` MEANS THERE IS NONE — never that the catalog
forgot to look — and a renderer must say the difference out loud.
`models_public: true` says this provider's models list answers WITHOUT a
credential. It exists because `orc extra ping`'s cheapest rung treats a 200
on /models as verification, and on a provider whose list is public that would
mark a profile verified with a garbage key. Such a row fills models_seen and
then falls THROUGH to the paid rung; the free answer is recorded as
`models-public` and is never the profile's verification.
`credential` on a cli row says how that tool takes a key, because the two
shipped ones are opposites: codex accepts a key on stdin and in an env var,
opencode's own login always prompts and cannot be driven — so ORC injects the
key into the child's environment instead and NEVER writes another tool's
credential store. `orc extra keyhelp` renders which of the three routes
applies.

providers.label: DeepSeek
providers.notes: Peak / off-peak rates differ; the off-peak window is the cheap one.

providers.label: Z.ai (GLM)
providers.notes: GLM Coding Plan is a subscription; a plan key and an API key are not the same credential.

providers.label: MiniMax
providers.notes: A key issued in one region does NOT work against the other region's host.

providers.label: Alibaba Qwen (DashScope)
providers.notes: DashScope's OpenAI-compatible mode already carries /v1 in the base; models_path is /models.

providers.label: Xiaomi MiMo
providers.notes: Open weights; a self-hosted deployment is the `custom` row, not this one.

providers.label: SiliconFlow
providers.notes: An AGGREGATOR: the model id names an upstream. Verify model_reported on every return.

providers.label: OpenRouter
providers.notes: An AGGREGATOR with TWO fallback kinds. Model-level fallback changes the model id (visible). Provider-level fallback is ON BY DEFAULT and KEEPS the model id while changing who serves it — visible only on engine `api`, via the response's `provider` field.

providers.label: Ollama (local)
providers.notes: Local: nothing leaves the machine, and the credential is a placeholder. Its /v1/messages REJECTS x-api-key, which is why auth_env is ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN and must stay that way.

providers.label: OpenCode
providers.notes: A LOCAL agentic CLI, so the thing that can be absent is the binary, not a URL. It reports token counts but NEVER which model answered — a substitution is invisible on this engine, and every render says so.

credential.note: opencode reads a key from the environment or a .env file at startup, so ORC injects it into the child process and never touches ~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json. `opencode auth login` has no flag for the key itself and always prompts — it cannot be driven, and ORC says so rather than pretending.

providers.label: Codex
providers.notes: CLI-only: there is no endpoint to point ORC at, which is why no_install_alternative is null. Custom providers live in the USER-level ~/.codex/config.toml, which ORC reads and NEVER writes. `-m` alone does not set the compute budget — the dispatch always passes `-c model_reasoning_effort` too, and an unsupported level is coerced SILENTLY, so the effort is reported as requested and never as confirmed.

credential.note: Every codex login path reads the key from STDIN and never from an argument — the tool's own docs say so, which is ORC's rule arrived at independently. CODEX_API_KEY scopes a key to ONE invocation and writes nothing global, so it is the default route.

providers.label: OpenCode Zen
providers.notes: The install-free route to the same catalogue: an ordinary OpenAI-compatible endpoint, reachable with a key and no local tool at all. Its /models answers WITHOUT a credential, which is why models_public is set — the free rung proves the URL and nothing else here.

providers.label: Custom endpoint
providers.notes: You supply the base URL and the auth shape. This row is why the catalog is not a gate.
